Researchers searched databases, including PubMed, Embase and Cochrane databases, and manually selected relevant randomized controlled trials.
To determine whether perioperative administration of dexmedetomidine reduces the incidence of postoperative delirium in adult patients undergoing cardiac surgery.

The studies included in this review were only randomized controlled trials. The following inclusion criteria were met: (1) Adult patients following cardiac surgery. (2) Patients with dexmedetomidine or placebo (normal saline). (3) Outcomes Indicators: Delirium incidence, ICU-days, Mortality.
Meta-analysis was performed using RevMan5.4.
We conducted a pragmatic, randomized, double-blind, parallel group, placebo-controlled trial.
Before surgery, patients were randomly assigned (1:1), by local investigators, either in the dexmedetomidine group or the placebo group using a dedicated and protected website (CSOnline; Clinsight).

Eligible patients were randomized into two groups. Dexmedetomidine (DEX) was administered during anesthesia and early postoperative period for patients in the DEX group, whereas normal saline was administered in the same rate for the same duration for patients in the control (CTRL) group.
and the present report follows the CONSORT 2010 guidelines for reporting parallel group randomized trials.
Patients were randomly allocated to the intervention or placebo group by assigning them the sequentially numbered envelope with the lowest numeration.
Sixty-four patients who underwent elective cardiac surgery under general anesthesia were shifted to intensive care unit (ICU) and randomly divided into two groups.
Group A (<italic>n</italic> = 32) received a 12 h infusion of normal saline and group B (<italic>n</italic> = 32) received a 12 h infusion of dexmedetomidine 0.4 μg/kg/h.

This single-centre, parallel-arm, randomised, placebo-controlled superiority trial was performed at Massachusetts General Hospital, an urban tertiary care teaching hospital in Boston, MA, with a cardiac surgical volume of approximately 1300 patients annually.
Participants were randomised to receive either intravenous dexmedetomidine or placebo in a 1:1 ratio using permuted block randomisation.
DECADE was an investigator-initiated, multicentre, double-blind trial with parallel design and superiority outcomes.
Consenting patients were randomly assigned 1:1, to dexmedetomidine or normal saline placebo.
We used a computer‐generated pseudorandom sequence to allocate participants to saline placebo or dexmedetomidine at a ratio of 1:1, using a permuted block size of 2 or 4.

We infused saline or 0.6 μg kg<sup>−1</sup> dexmedetomidine (Jiangsu Hengrui Medicine, Jiangsu, China) over 10 min and then a continuous infusion of saline or dexmedetomidine 0.4 μg.kg<sup>−1</sup>.h<sup>−1</sup> until the end of surgery.

outcome: Postoperative delirium as defined and ascertained by each trial.
